observations.observation: ASML’s FY2025 results and initial FY2026 sales outlook were public by Jan. 28: the company reported €32.7 billion in net sales, €9.6 billion in net income, and an initial €34–39 billion outlook. AP’s same-day report also noted a planned workforce reduction of about 1,700 and export-control context.
observations.publication_time: 2026-01-28 (ASML source listing shows 07:00 without timezone; AP report timestamp 09:15:20Z)
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The company reports primary figures in euros; dollar conversions depend on exchange-rate convention. AP’s workforce and export-control context does not alter the company’s reported financial values.

observations.observation: The public guidance baseline changed in two steps: ASML set 2026 net-sales guidance at €34–39 billion in January, raised it to €36–40 billion in April, then to €43–45 billion in July. The July release also reported Q2 sales of €9.326 billion and 54.0% gross margin; Reuters reported the July change as the second increase of the year.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: ASML’s April release said its guidance range accommodated potential outcomes of ongoing export-control discussions. Sales guidance and capacity plans are forward-looking; they are not realized results.

observations.observation: Intel’s FY2025 Form 10-K reported revenue of $52.9 billion and a net loss attributable to Intel of $267 million. These full-year figures were publicly available well before the September case message.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: This annual filing supports revenue and net-loss figures; the specific free-cash-flow and stock-based-compensation percentages in the article were not independently verified in the retrieved passages.

observations.observation: Intel’s July Q2 release reported revenue up 25% year over year and GAAP gross margin of 40.4% versus 27.5%; the next-day 10-Q showed Foundry revenue was $5.765 billion, including $293 million external revenue, and the segment had a $2.089 billion operating loss. The 10-Q also attributed client revenue growth partly to higher ASPs while client volume was down 8%, and noted supply constraints.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: These figures separate company-wide growth from Foundry’s external revenue and loss, and identify price/mix and supply effects; they do not establish the cause of the Q2 GAAP net loss.
